items.headline: Rena Lee becomes the first Singaporean elected a judge of the International Court of Justice
items.summary: Ambassador-for-International-Law Rena Lee, 57, won an ICJ seat in the first round on 3 November, taking 151 of 191 UN General Assembly votes and 13 of 15 in the Security Council. She is the first Singaporean and first Southeast Asian woman on the court; her term runs 2027-2036.

items.headline: Singaporean man jailed for life for starving and beating his teenage sister to death
items.summary: Huang Bocan was sentenced to life imprisonment for the 2021 killing of his 19-year-old sister, Huang Baoying, whom he starved and beat over several months at their Clementi flat.

items.headline: Singaporean, 29, jailed five years and nine months for killing a cyclist who stole his backpack
items.summary: A 29-year-old Singaporean was sentenced to five years and nine months' jail for running over and killing a cyclist who had snatched his backpack while he was on holiday in Australia.

items.headline: Man, 27, posed as a woman on dating apps to lure victims into rigged mahjong games
items.summary: A 27-year-old man was jailed for two years on 5 November for posing as a woman on dating apps to lure men into rigged mahjong games, where accomplices cheated them out of their money.

items.headline: Cyclone Murasu kills at least eight in Andhra Pradesh and causes heavy crop damage
items.summary: Cyclone Murasu crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole early on 3 November with winds up to 120kmph, killing at least eight people. CM N. Chandrababu Naidu put the damage at about Rs 1,918 crore, with crops hit across roughly 143,000 hectares; it was the region's second cyclone in a week.

items.headline: Thousands rally in Delhi demanding the resignation of India's election chief
items.summary: Opposition supporters led by Rahul Gandhi rallied in New Delhi demanding that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls that they say enables voter deletions. The Election Commission denies favouring any party.

items.headline: Update: Russell Brand jailed for 10 and a half years for rape and sexual assault
items.summary: Russell Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months at Southwark Crown Court on 9 November, days after a jury convicted him of one rape and three sexual assaults. Judge Bennathan called him a sexual predator; Brand becomes eligible for release after serving about two-thirds of the term.

items.headline: At least 34 die as a migrant boat sinks off Senegal
items.summary: At least 34 people died when a small boat sank off the Senegalese coast, with one person rescued as the search continued. A Senegalese human-rights group demanded government action over the repeated Atlantic-route sinkings.

items.headline: Update: US and Iran negotiate quietly to avert a wider war as Trump holds off on new strikes
items.summary: The United States and Iran are negotiating indirectly through Qatari and Pakistani mediators to avoid a return to all-out war, as President Trump said fresh strikes were 'highly unlikely' if talks progress on Iran's nuclear programme and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran says talks could resume within two days if Washington lifts its blockade and sanctions.

items.headline: Anthropic launches its Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models ahead of a planned IPO
items.summary: Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and a restricted Mythos 5.2, cutting Fable's input price to about US$8 per million tokens from $10 and reserving Mythos for vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences users. The company said the launch came days before its planned IPO in the week of 16 November.

items.headline: AI hardware startup Nominal triples its valuation to US$3 billion in eight months
items.summary: Nominal raised a $240 million Series C led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and co-led by Insight Partners, valuing the AI-hardware company at $3 billion, roughly triple its valuation from a round eight months earlier.

items.headline: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI-agent security startup Clutch for about US$500 million
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks is negotiating to acquire Clutch, a startup that secures AI agents, for roughly $500 million, about 50 times its annual recurring revenue, amid a wave of dealmaking for agent-security firms.

items.headline: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor to run parallel agent workspaces
items.summary: Meta bought Conductor, whose tool spins up software projects by deploying multiple AI agents across parallel workspaces. Conductor's standalone cloud service will shut down on 20 November.

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds from its AI-driven rout as the Dow jumps more than 1,100 points
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged about 1,104 points (2.15%) and the S&P 500 posted its best day since April, recovering from the prior week's AI-led sell-off. The Nasdaq rose 2.74% and the VIX fell about 22%, though Nvidia lagged, falling around 4%.

items.headline: Coherent soars on blowout AI-optics earnings, leading a broad tech rally
items.summary: Coherent was among the top S&P 500 gainers, climbing double digits after reporting fiscal first-quarter revenue up about 50% to $2.37 billion on surging data-centre optics demand and raising its guidance. Bloom Energy and Flex also rose sharply.

items.headline: Gold firms and oil tumbles after Trump plays down fresh strikes on Iran
items.summary: Spot gold rose about 0.7% to around US$4,094 an ounce while oil fell sharply after President Trump said renewed strikes on Iran were unlikely, easing inflation fears. Traders still price an about 81% chance of a December Federal Reserve rate increase ahead of US inflation data this week.

items.headline: Verstappen clings to second over Russell as Formula 1 heads to Las Vegas
items.summary: With Kimi Antonelli already confirmed as 2026 world champion and Mercedes having clinched the constructors' crown in Brazil, Max Verstappen holds second on 279 points, 17 ahead of George Russell, with three rounds left. The Las Vegas Grand Prix runs on 21 November.

items.headline: Gauff beats Pegula as the season-ending WTA Finals get under way in Indian Wells
items.summary: The WTA Finals began on 8 November in Indian Wells, California, moved from Riyadh for this year, with Coco Gauff opening her round-robin campaign by beating Jessica Pegula. The semi-finals are set for 14 November and the final for 15 November.

items.headline: The Rubin Observatory may have found the solar system's sixth dwarf planet
items.summary: Astronomers using the Vera C. Rubin Observatory reported a new dwarf-planet candidate beyond Neptune, provisionally designated 2026 ED138, with an estimated diameter between 600 and 1,500 kilometres. If confirmed, it would join the five bodies already recognised as dwarf planets.

items.headline: UK coverage runs short in today's edition
items.summary: Beyond the Brand sentencing, reachable outlets surfaced little fresh verifiable UK-domestic news in the past 48 hours; BBC and Sky News were not reachable, and fallback outlets carried mostly continuations of earlier stories.

fun_fact.headline: The shortest war in history lasted about 38 minutes
fun_fact.body: The shortest war in recorded history lasted well under an hour. On 27 August 1896 the Royal Navy bombarded the sultan's palace in Zanzibar to force out a ruler Britain opposed, and his forces surrendered almost at once. By most accounts the fighting, from the first shell to the ceasefire, ran for only about 38 minutes.
fun_fact.source: History Hit / Historic UK / History Today

puzzle.title: Counting the Squares
puzzle.body: Picture a large square divided into a 4x4 grid of 16 small equal squares. How many squares of any size (1x1, 2x2, 3x3 or 4x4) can you find in the whole figure?
puzzle.approach: Count by size, not just the little boxes, then add the sizes together.

word_puzzle.title: Boxed In
word_puzzle.body: Letter Boxed. Top: V I G; Right: O A S; Bottom: T P C; Left: N R H. Words of 3+ letters; consecutive letters from different sides; each new word starts with the previous word's last letter; use all 12 letters in two words.
word_puzzle.approach: Chain two words that together use all 12 letters; the second starts with the first word's last letter.
word_puzzle.answer: VOTING -> GRAPHICS (uses all 12 letters; no step stays on the same side).

notes: Thin news cycle (9 Nov was Deepavali, a quiet Singapore news day) plus a degraded compile-environment search index: many allowed primary outlets (Straits Times, CNA, BBC, Sky News, The Hindu and other Indian primary outlets, Reuters) were unreachable/blocked and their deep URLs did not surface. India ran on the authorized fallback tier (Al Jazeera). UK ran on fallback (CNN) plus a placeholder card. Several sections fell below the 4-item floor because reachable allowed/fallback outlets were genuinely exhausted for fresh, non-duplicate, deep-linked stories: India (2), UK (1 + placeholder), Global (2), Business (3), Sports (2), Misc (1). Total verified items across the brief: 19, well above the 8-item hard-stop. Sports is between F1 rounds (Las Vegas GP is 21 Nov); the India-NZ 3rd ODI was being played on 10 Nov with no result yet, and the ATP Finals had not started (15 Nov) - so Sports carried the F1 runner-up picture and the opening of the WTA Finals. Confirmed-but-unlinked (dropped for lack of an allowed-outlet deep URL in this environment): the Russia-Ukraine-US Abu Dhabi peace talks convening 10-11 Nov, the COP31 climate summit opening in Antalya, and the Mars/Alba Mons hydrogen-chloride volcanism finding. Previous edition for 2026-11-09 exists; no missed run.
